source_text: Nemo ergo vos seducat nec se negent impii ista sentire, sed, si verum dicunt, aut audientia detur aut certe isti ipsi episcopi, qui nunc dissident, damnent quae supra dixi cum Manichaeis ista tenere, sicut nos ista damnamus quae de nobis iactant, et fit plena concordia. Quod si nolunt, scitote eos esse Manichaeos, et ab eorum vos abstinete consortiis.
pass_a_gloss: Let no one therefore seduce you, nor let the ungodly deny that they hold these things; but if they speak truly, either let a hearing be given, or certainly let these very bishops who now dissent condemn the things which I said above they hold with the Manichaeans, just as we condemn the things they toss against us, and full concord comes about. But if they are unwilling, know that they are Manichaeans, and keep yourselves from their fellowships.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Let no one deceive you, then, and let the ungodly not deny that they hold these opinions. If they are telling the truth, either let us have a hearing, or let these very bishops who now disagree condemn the positions which, as I have said above, they hold along with the Manichaeans—just as we condemn the things they allege against us. Then there will be complete agreement. If they refuse, know that they are Manichaeans, and refrain from sharing fellowship with them.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
